summary: Rewrite 2 Re tr(diag(w)(g − 1)) as Re tr(diag(w)(g − 1)(1 − g⁻¹)), expand both sides into double sums over the entries, and compare term by term, using g⁻¹ = diag(ε)gᴴdiag(ε).

steps.claim: It suffices to prove the inequality with 2 Re tr(diag(w)(g − 1)) replaced by Re tr(diag(w)(g − 1)(1 − g⁻¹)); the two numbers are equal (step 5, proved last).

steps.lean: simp [frobenius_norm_sq_eq_sum, trace, mul_sum, ← sum_add_distrib, blockDiagPart, eq_comm]
steps.claim: Expanding the Frobenius norms and the traces entrywise (a_ε(g)_ij = g_ij if ε_i = ε_j and 0 otherwise), both sides become double sums over (i, j): on the left Σ_{i,j} [a v_i²|(g − 1)_ij|² + w_i Re((g − 1)_ij(1 − g⁻¹)_ji)], on the right Σ_{i,j} 2C·[ε_i ≠ ε_j]·|g_ij|².

steps.lean: gcongr with i _ j; cases h i j
steps.claim: Compare the double sums term by term: fix i, j and split the hypothesis h(i, j) into a·v_i² ≤ w_i and (ε_i ≠ ε_j → w_i ≤ C).

steps.lean:
split_ifs <;> simp_all [mul_right_comm, ← cast_mul, mul_pow,
    Complex.sq_norm, normSq, signMatrix, U.inv_mat] <;> nlinarith
steps.claim: Each term, by cases on ε_i = ε_j and on i = j, using g⁻¹ = diag(ε)gᴴdiag(ε), so that (1 − g⁻¹)_ji = δ_ij − ε_iε_j·conj(g_ij): if ε_i = ε_j the term equals (a v_i² − w_i)|(g − 1)_ij|² ≤ 0 = right-hand term; if ε_i ≠ ε_j (so i ≠ j) it equals (a v_i² + w_i)|g_ij|², which is at most 2C|g_ij|² because a v_i² ≤ w_i ≤ C. Each case is closed by nlinarith.

steps.lean:
simp [↓mul_sub, ↓sub_mul, ↓Units.mul_inv, trace, signMatrix, U.inv_mat, mul_right_comm,
    ← cast_mul]; ring
steps.claim: The identity of step 1: (g − 1)(1 − g⁻¹) = (g − 1) + (g⁻¹ − 1), and Re tr(diag(w)(g⁻¹ − 1)) = Re tr(diag(w)(g − 1)), because g⁻¹ = diag(ε)gᴴdiag(ε), diag(ε) commutes with diag(w) and squares to 1, and tr(diag(w)(gᴴ − 1)) is the complex conjugate of tr(diag(w)(g − 1)); hence 2 Re tr(diag(w)(g − 1)) = Re tr(diag(w)(g − 1)(1 − g⁻¹)).
